HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Matches CallingBell.cs:21. Worth noting against the same batch's relic/byrdpip, which drops the identical declaration.

AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and G3 per binding rule 4. The curse half is faithful; the relic half implements the source's TEST-MODE branch, so it grants three fixed relics instead of three pool pulls (G1), consumes none of the three Rewards draws those pulls cost (G2), and auto-keeps what the game offers as a skippable screen (G3, now also a gap -- re-verdicted by the 2026-07-26 fix pass).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the port implements CallingBell.GenerateRewards' `TestMode.IsOn` branch, not the shipping branch
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CallingBell.cs:34-64 has two arms. The `if (TestMode.IsOn)` arm (lines 39-52) builds three RelicRewards with FIXED models -- Anchor, Gremlin Horn, Mummified Hand. The shipping arm (53-63) builds `new RelicReward(RelicRarity.Common, Owner)`, `(RelicRarity.Uncommon, ...)` and `(RelicRarity.Rare, ...)`, each of which resolves its relic in RelicReward.Populate via `RelicFactory.PullNextRelicFromFront(Player, rarity)` (RelicReward.cs:75-96). calling_bell.py:21 hard-codes `RELICS = ('anchor', 'gremlin_horn', 'mummified_hand')` -- the test arm. TestMode.IsOn is a unit-test flag: `TestMode.TurnOnInternal` (TestMode.cs:38) is documented 'NEVER CALL THIS. Only calls should be in NetCoreRunner and CiCoreRunner' and has no caller anywhere under src/, so the shipping game always takes the second arm. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): `run.add_relic('calling_bell')` yields relics ['calling_bell', 'anchor', 'gremlin_horn', 'mummified_hand'] on every seed, where the game yields one random Common, one Uncommon and one Rare from the run's grab bag. Both sides ported: Calling Bell is granted by the ported Darv shrine (events/darv.py) and the sim has a working rarity pull (`RunState.pull_relic_from_front`, run.py:559-566, used by the elite-relic reward path). This is not a dormancy question at all -- the wrong relics are granted in every run that takes the Bell.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the three PullNextRelicFromFront draws are never consumed
guards.issue: MECHANISM: each of the shipping arm's three RelicRewards burns a pull from the player's relic grab bag when it Populates, and (per the project's own note, recorded in memory as 'Relic rarity rolls on Rewards') PullNextRelicFromFront also burns a per-player Rewards stream draw. The sim's port takes neither. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): `grab bag 96 -> 96` across add_relic('calling_bell'). Two observables, not one: the three relics the Bell gives are wrong (G1) AND every subsequent relic pull in the run is shifted, because the pool it draws from still contains three relics the game would have removed. Filed separately from G1 because fixing G1 by granting three random relics without going through run.pull_relic_from_front would leave this half broken.

guards.what: G3: RewardsCmd.OfferCustom is a take-or-skip reward screen; the port grants all three unconditionally
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the take-or-skip seam exists and this site uses it. `RunState.offer_relic` (sts2_rl/run.py:475-496) and `RunState.offer_potion` (sts2_rl/run.py:498-506) are the port of RewardsCmd.OfferCustom's declinable RelicReward / PotionReward: they consult `run.reward_selector` (the driver surfaces it as a REWARD_RELIC / REWARD_POTION decision) and only call add_relic / add_potion on a take, so a declined relic never runs its AfterObtained -- RelicReward.OnSelect (RelicReward.cs:109-115) is the only path to RelicCmd.Obtain. sts2_rl/relics/calling_bell.py offers each of the three through `run.offer_relic`. WAS: the port granted all three unconditionally.

guards.what: G4: `Hook.ShouldAddToDeck` is consulted by CardPileCmd.Add (CardPileCmd.cs:384) on the curse; the sim has no such hook
guards.rationale: VOCABULARY RULING (2026-07-26 relic fix pass), applied at every dead-in-the-source site in this tier so it stops contradicting itself. When a C# member the sim omits is DEAD IN THE GAME SOURCE ITSELF -- zero overrides, zero producers, zero callers anywhere under src/ -- the correct verdict is `faithful`, not `waiver`. PROMPT.md v6 item 3, which the relic stream itself wrote, settles the principle for the mirror-image case: 'a waiver is in-scope-adjacent and declined, and here there is no source behaviour to be faithful to.' A waiver claims something in scope was deliberately not audited; here there is nothing to decline, because the member provably cannot fire in any run of the shipping game and cannot become live by porting more content -- it would take a change to the game's own source. `faithful` also states the stronger and more useful fact: the two codebases have the SAME observable. Before this pass the relic tier split 8 waivers against 5 faithfuls on identical reasoning; these entries are now all `faithful` (binding rule 3). NOTE: this ruling does NOT touch MULTIPLAYER gates (`player != base.Owner`, `Players.Count == 1`), which stay `waiver` -- the shared contract names multiplayer as out of scope outright, and unlike a dead member a player count really can differ in the shipping game; the sim simply does not model that mode. AT THIS SITE: The finding is unchanged and still executed: `grep -rn should_add_to_deck sts2_rl/ --include=*.py` returns ZERO hits, and on the C# side `grep -rn ShouldAddToDeck src/` returns exactly four lines -- the dispatch at CardPileCmd.cs:384, the Hook wrapper at Hook.cs:2084-2088 and the `public virtual` base declaration at AbstractModel.cs:2144. Not one override exists in the whole game, so the hook is dead code in C# too, not unported content. ONLY THE VERDICT CHANGES. Rule 7: CardPileCmd.cs, Hook.cs and AbstractModel.cs are not hashed here.

AddCurseToDeck asserts the card is a Curse, creates it on the run, and routes it through `Add(card, PileType.Deck)` (CardPileCmd.cs:1037-1056). run.add_card (run.py:341-354) runs modify_card_being_added_to_deck before the append and after_card_added_to_deck after it, which are the two deck-add hooks the sim models. The curse is ported and correct: cards/curse_of_the_bell.py is CardType.CURSE, eternal=True, max_upgrade_level 0. EXECUTED: the probe reports `curse added: ['curse_of_the_bell']`.

guards.what: N2: the ORDER -- curse first, relics second
guards.rationale: CallingBell.cs:29-31 adds the curse, waits, then offers; calling_bell.py:26-28 adds the curse then the relics. Recorded because it is load-bearing for any granted relic that reacts to the deck: Mummified Hand and Gremlin Horn do not, but a fixed G1 pulling a random Common could pull one that does (e.g. a deck-size reader), and the curse must already be in the deck when it lands.

RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
